title: Interactive Knowledge Visualization
definition: A system that allows for dynamic visualization and exploration of complex interconnected concepts.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of it like a map that lets you zoom in and out and click on things to learn more about them. It helps you understand how different ideas are connected.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Interactive knowledge visualization is a method of representing data in a graph-like structure, allowing users to explore and understand relationships between concepts. In this context, it refers to the CADMIES Mycelium Map.
difficulty_levels.expert: Interactive knowledge visualization is a novel method of exploring complex systems, combining principles from graph theory, human-computer interaction, and educational technology. It allows for the representation and navigation of large, interconnected datasets. In this context, the CADMIES Mycelium Map serves as a unique example of interactive knowledge visualization, providing insights into the interplay between various philosophical concepts.

extra_fields.insight: The CADMIES Mycelium Map is an interactive system that allows users to explore and understand the complex interconnections between philosophical concepts.
